Dagmar.biography:
Dagmar plays himself as a generally cheerful presence — an overconfidence that is both specific (that a given scheme will ultimately lead to a positive outcome) and general (that the Criamon vision for universal redemption will inevitably succeed). He tries to embody the virtues of his house, non-violence and vegetarianism chief among them. Because he believes the Criamon vision's success is inevitable, the only real question left is how large a role he gets to play in it — and delving into the magical mysteries of the North Sea is his chance to make that contribution his own. He treats his own magical wisdom and power as central to that goal, and if other, less enlightened parties get in the way, he feels he has considerable flexibility in dealing with them: if someone won't sell something the vision needs, other means of acquisition might be justified, since ultimately it serves their interest too.

The Ghostly Warder: A few years before the campaign began, on an errand for Solving in Sweden, Dagmar heard a folk superstition about a set of standing stones further inland — that they would gift chosen members of the community with enhanced senses. Suspecting Faerie involvement, he went to investigate alone, but found instead a powerful magical aura. Confident this was something he was equipped to handle, he told his companions to stay behind and went in by himself. Unknowingly, he had stumbled into a regio at the center of the stones. He spent a happy first day exploring it — and then couldn't find his way out. By the third day, with nothing but grass and dew to sustain him, he was preparing himself for death. That was when the spirit of the glen took pity on him: not a follower of the local tradition and by rights unworthy of its blessing, Dagmar had nonetheless been respectful of the stones and clearly sought only to observe and learn. The spirit manifested an aspect to him and offered to guide him out, in exchange for services to be specified later. Dagmar agreed — the decision for the aspect to keep following him afterward was something of an impulse on the spirit's part, equal parts fondness for his curiosity and the recognition that the same curiosity could easily get him killed before it collected on the debt. Dagmar's own takeaway was narrower: he sought out and learned Piercing the Magic Veil, so he'd be better equipped to find his way out of a regio next time.

Dagmar's answers to the Criamon riddles:

"If I wear a mask and none see beneath it, do I still exist?" — Yes, for the flesh behind the mask still moves it. The forces behind the effects we can see may be invisible, but they are no less real.

"A tree that stands for a hundred years and a flower that blooms for a day — which has lived longer?" — They have both lived the same amount of time, since, as the circle of time repeats, the tree will be reborn as the flower and the flower as the tree. All beings are the same age, and that age is infinite.

"What can bend the infinite?" — Magic. Only through magic can one create an escape from the infinite cycle of time.

"I built a house of wind and it held my breath. Why did it collapse when I exhaled?" — The house was created by attachment to the ephemeral, but eventually, inevitably, returned to its natural form and dissipated. In the same way, all attachments are fleeting — lasting for a time but ultimately returning to pure chaos, and later to pure order, as the cycle of time continues. Holding onto such things may make them last a while, but eventually one must release them, and once released they will be no more. The cultivation of material wealth is, therefore, ultimately a pointless endeavor.

Dagmar walks the Path of Seeming — fitting for his cerebral nature and focus on Intellego. His tattoos, marking that path, run along his neck, hidden under an unusually high collar in ordinary company. His fascination with magical regiones runs deeper than the usual Hermetic interest in vis and research: since the Hypostasis is so often found near strong magical activity, he suspects that high-magic-aura places may sit somehow "closer" to it — and that regiones might be the one route by which people without the Gift could ever escape the tyranny of linear time, the way a magus might eventually reach the Hypostasis through their own studies. Even now, years past his own Gauntlet, he's continued acting as Solving's assistant more than as an independent magus in his own right — a position he finds comfortable, and part of why he still frames his current role as "keeping Solving's seat warm" rather than truly making the covenant his own.

Éogan Dobhartha.biography:
A magus from Hibernia with a strong connection to water magic. Éogan was taken from his home as part of a political treaty and apprenticed into the Order against his will — now he seeks a fresh start, aiming to build a new life far from his past.

Éogan hails from Connacht, in the west of Hibernia — one of the last places in Europe where non-Hermetic magi still practice openly, free of the Order's harassment, thanks to the 300-year-old Treaty of Cnoc Maol Réidh. Under its terms, the magicians of Connacht must surrender seven of their own Gifted youths at each Hibernian Tribunal. Éogan was one of them: as a child, magicians of the Coill Trí, unwilling to give up any of their own apprentices, came to his village and made his parents an offer they couldn't refuse. He was taken away kicking and screaming, and apprenticed to the Order against his will.

His parens turned out to be a magus of House Ex Miscellanea, master of a very old Irish tradition that was nonetheless on the verge of dying out. The two of them spent most of their time traveling Ireland, visiting magical sites and finding water for the locals and their cattle. Looking back, Éogan thinks his apprenticeship was as much about finding someone to care for the man in his final years as it was about preserving the tradition — his aging master, kindly but often slow and meandering in his teaching, was approaching the end of his life and needed help with the day-to-day work of his vocation. In winter, the two would stay at his master's covenant, where the other magi quietly helped fill in the gaps in Éogan's education.

A year before his Gauntlet, Éogan attended the Hibernian Tribunal and met Solving Epicurusson for the first time — and knew immediately what he wanted to do once his apprenticeship ended. His master didn't live to see him inducted into the Order; a fellow covenant member saw the last portion of his training through. With most of his ties to the past already gone, Éogan left his homeland and never looked back.

Personality: Éogan has spent much of his life feeling abandoned, lonely, and powerless. He's eager now to start over, shed his old identity, and rebuild — quiet but determined, curious about the world, ready to make something of himself so people stop looking down on him. He likes to keep to himself, but also yearns for deep, lasting friendships.

The Well Dreams: Éogan has a recurring dream — he dives into a deep well, swimming further and further down until the walls give way to a vast enclosure where the Queen of the Deep sits on her throne, surrounded by her Coral Court. In the dream he's a completely different person: a proud warrior, confident, beloved by everyone. Before he wakes, the Queen asks him a question he can never remember afterward. Sometimes he's offered gifts — usually small shells and pearls that hold Aquam vis, and which remain in his possession when he wakes. This is the nature of his personal vis source.

virtues.description: The Gift is a special Virtue, because it has no cost. The character suffers all the penalties of The Gift, just as magi do (see page @@), but can be taught Supernatural Abilities without having to take the corresponding Virtues (see page @@ for rules). virtues.description: Your magic lineage and traditions are from the druids and the vanquished former house of Diedne, making you especially skilled with Spontaneous magic. When you cast a spontaneous spell without expending Fatigue, you may choose to divide by five or by two. virtues.name: Hermetic Magus
virtues.description: You are a member of the Order of Hermes. All magi must take this as their Social Status, and only magi may take it.

virtues.name: Apt Student
virtues.description:
You are particularly good at learning from others. 

When being taught or trained by someone else, add five to the Source Quality.

virtues.name: Common Sense
virtues.description: Whenever you are about to do something contrary to what is sensible in the game setting, common sense (the storyguide) alerts you to the error. This is an excellent Virtue for a beginning player, as it legitimizes any help the storyguide may give.

virtues.name: Faerie Blood
virtues.description:
Somewhere in your ancestry there is a faerie, and this relation gives you an intuitive grasp of the motivations and personalities of those supernatural folk. Faeries are more comfortable around you than around other humans, and given time, may even forget the mortal blood in your veins.

 You are resistant to aging, and get –1 to all aging rolls.

 Type of Faerie Blood (pick one, or create a simil

virtues.name: Inspirational
virtues.description:
You are a stirring speaker or a heroic 

figure, and can urge people to great efforts. You give targets a +3 bonus to rolls for appropriate Personality Traits.

virtues.name: Self-confident
virtues.description:
You ha

ve firm confidence in your own abilities, and have a Confidence Score of two. You also start with five Confidence Points, rather than the usual three. (See page @@ for Confidence rules.)

virtues.name: Unaging
virtues.description: You do not suffer the effects of age. In game terms, your aging points do not decrease your Characteristics, only building up to give you Decrepitude points. If a crisis is not potentially fatal, you suffer no ill-effects. You may die from terminal and potentially fatal crises, according to the normal rules. You are not enfeebled when you reach four Decrepitude points, but you die as normal when y

virtues.name: Venus's Blessing
virtues.description: People are often attracted to you. You get +3 on Communication and Presence rolls with sexually compatible characters in appropriate situations. At times you can put this to good use. At other times it’s an annoyance.

flaws.name: Chaotic Magic
flaws.description: Your magic is very wild. When you cast a spontaneous spell, you must specify a desired level of effect. If you fall short of or exceed that target by more than one level, the spell still works, but its effects are beyond your control—the storyguide decides the results. The level of effect includes any levels you assign to Penetration.

flaws.name: Difficult Longevity Ritual
flaws.description: Something in your magical nature makes it difficult to create an effective Longevity Ritual for you. Anyone (including yourself) creating a Longevity Ritual for you must halve their Lab Total. You may create Longevity Rituals for others without penalty.

flaws.name: Magic Addiction
flaws.description: You crave the rush of casting and holding power over magic. Whenever you cast a spell, you have a difficult time stopping yourself from casting again and again until you drop from exhaustion. Whenever you use a stress die in spellcasting, you must, whether or not the spell succeeds, make an Intelligence + Concentration stress roll, against an Ease Factor of half the level of the spell (or, if you

flaws.name: Twilight Prone
flaws.description: You either enjoy or cannot help running excessive amounts of magic through you when you cast spells. You must roll to resist Twilight on a single magical botch, rather than on a double botch like most magi.

flaws.name: Lycanthrope
flaws.description: You have been cursed to change form into a dangerous predator (such as a wolf, lynx, or bear) on nights of the full moon (or similar, monthly, astrological events). No items or clothing transform between shapes, and it takes one full round for the full transformation to take effect. You are not immune to normal weapons, and the curse does not infect bite victims. The animal may be detected as a cu

flaws.name: Dark Secret
flaws.description: You are haunted by something that would lead to shame, rejection, and possibly revenge if discovered. Hints about the secret continually arise, and there might be others who know it and could betray you. This makes you avoid certain places, dislike certain people, or fear certain things.

flaws.name: Feud
flaws.description: Your family is involved in a feud. The opposing family or families are roughly of equivalent strength to your family and its allies. You are liable to be ambushed or attacked by opposing clansmen, and your family expects you to join raids against your enemies.

flaws.name: Visions
flaws.description: You often see images related to emotionally or magically laden events. A vision might be of the past, a possible future, or a distant occurrence, and is often symbolic or confusing. Visions usually come to you at quiet times or in places connected with a powerful emotional or magical event, such as the site of a patricide or diabolic sacrifice. Your visions may warn you of dangers to come, or get

flaws.name: Ambitious - Minor
flaws.description: You want to be the most successful or powerful person in the world in some respect. You will not be distracted into doing things that do not contribute to your ambition, and are very eager to do things that advance it.

flaws.name: Avaricious - Major
flaws.description: You want money, lots of money. When you have it, you do not spend it, but hoard it so that you can count it. You can be avaricious about physical things other than money, such as books or raw vis. In this case, you do not use the things you hoard, nor do you allow others to use them.

flaws.name: Driven (Major)
flaws.description: You have some goal which you are determined to bring about. This has to be the sort of big goal that could shape an entire life, but if you do accomplish it you will immediately turn to a new project.

flaws.name: Optimistic (Minor)
flaws.description: You are convinced that everything will turn out for the best. This is not overconfidence, as you accept that you might well fail. Even if you do, however, you are sure that circumstances will mean that everything works to your benefit.

flaws.name: Proud (Minor)
flaws.description: You believe that you are more important than just about everybody, and expect the appropriate respect. Magi may admit one or two equals, but do not believe that they have any superiors. Mundanes will admit social superiors, but still believe themselves to be fundamentally better than, say, the king.

flaws.name: Wrathful (Minor)
flaws.description: You are prone to anger over the smallest issues, and your rage when you are thwarted in something major is terrible to behold.

virtues.description: Your Advancement Totals for one Hermetic Art are increased by one half, rounded up. At character creation, any experience points you put into that Art are also increased by one half (rounded up), and you may exceed the normal recommended limits. You may take this Virtue twice, for two different Arts.

virtues.description: Your Advancement Totals for one Hermetic Art are increased by one half, rounded up. At character creation, any experience points you put into that Art are also increased by one half (rounded up), and you may exceed the normal recommended limits. You may take this Virtue twice, for two different Arts.

virtues.name: Inventive Genius
virtues.description:
Invention comes naturally to you. 

You get +3 to your Lab Total if you are not using a Laboratory Text or being taught. If you experiment, you get +6.

virtues.name: Minor Magical Focus
virtues.description:
Your magic is particularly attuned to some narrow field, such as self-transformation, birds of prey, or healing. In general, the field should be slightly narrower than a single Technique and Form combination, although it may include restricted areas of several such combinations. Healing, for example, is a part of Creo Corpus, Creo Animal, and possibly Creo 

Herbam. You cannot be focused on a labo

It does not apply when learning, teaching, or writing about the Art. You may take this Virtue twice, for two different Arts. virtues.name: Luck
virtues.description: You perform well in situations where luck is more of a factor than skill or talent. You get +1 to +3 (storyguide’s discretion) on rolls in such situations, depending upon how much luck is involved. You do well at games of chance, but may be labeled a cheater if you play them too often.

virtues.name: Great Intelligence
virtues.description: You may raise any Characteristic that already has a score of at least +3 by one point, to no more than +5. Make sure you describe what it is about you that causes that increase (such as sheer bulk, a lean build, or extreme charisma). You may take this Virtue twice for the same Characteristic, and for more than one Characteristic.

Make sure you describe what it is about you that causes that increase (such as sheer bulk, a lean build, or extreme charisma). You may take this Virtue twice for the same Characteristic, and for more than one Characteristic.

virtues.name: Cautious With Magic Theory
virtues.description: You are very careful with a specific Ability, and are less likely to fail spectacularly if you do fail when using it. You roll two fewer botch dice than normal whenever you are required to roll botch dice for that Ability. This may mean that you roll no botch dice. This Virtue may apply to any Ability, even one you cannot learn at character creation.

virtues.name: Affinity With Magic Theory
virtues.description: All Advancement Totals for one Ability are increased by half, rounded up, as are any experience points you put in that Ability at character creation. You may only take this Virtue once for a given Ability, but may take it again for different Abilities. virtues.description: You are particularly adept with one Ability, and add 2 to its value whenever you use it. Note that you do not, in general, use an Ability when learning it, writing about it, or helping someone else to improve it. You may only take this Virtue once for a given Ability, but may take it more than once for different Abilities.

flaws.name: Close Family Ties
flaws.description: Your family is one of the most important things in your life, and still supports and aids you whenever possible, even at personal risk. Family members do not hesitate to do you any favor that is within their power, and can call on their friends and neighbors to help you. It works both ways, however; your family will require help from you some day.

flaws.description: You are convinced that everything will turn out for the best. This is not overconfidence, as you accept that you might well fail. Even if you do, however, you are sure that circumstances will mean that everything works to your benefit.

flaws.name: Humble
flaws.description: You are humble, always willing to believe that others are more skilled and better than you. You do not necessarily underestimate your own abilities, you just think others are better.

flaws.name: Motion Sickness
flaws.description: Riding a horse, in a cart, or sailing on a ship makes you violently ill. When not traveling on foot, you suffer double the fatigue loss on long journeys, with a minimum loss of two Fatigue levels. Violent jostling over a period of a few hours could conceivably lead to unconsciousness.

flaws.name: Small Frame
flaws.description: You are of a lighter-than-average build. Your Size is reduced to –1. This means that the severity of wounds you take increases in four point increments, rather than five point. (See page @@). You cannot take this Flaw and Giant Blood (page @@), Large (page @@), or Dwarf (page @@).

spells.name: Maintaining the Demanding Spell
spells.description: You cast this spell on a spell that you have already cast and are maintaining through concentration. The spell that requires concentration is then automatically maintained for the duration of this spell, whether you concentrate or not. Valerian de Castellane.name: Valerian de Castellane
Valerian de Castellane.biography: Solving had a ship earmarked for Valerian — a fellow Guernicus mage — as far back as the fleet's founding years, but stood him up on the arrangement before vanishing into Twilight in 1220. Whatever fell apart between them left Valerian exposed enough to end up imprisoned by the Duke of Brabant not long after. He was eventually rescued, and the ship — what became the Adamant — didn't actually reach him until 1222, delivered by a covenant under new leadership making good on an old promise.

virtues.name: Mastered Spells
virtues.description: You have fifty experience points to spend on mastering spells that you know. (See page @@ for rules on mastering spells.) You may take this Virtue if you also have Flawless Magic, to give you more experience points to spend on mastering your spells. You may take this Virtue multiple times.

virtues.name: Quiet Magic
virtues.description:
You can cast spells using only a soft voice at no penalty, and at only a –5 penalty if you do not speak at all. You gain no benefits from using your voice normally but gain the normal benefit for using a booming voice. The range of Voice Range spells is determined normally, based on how loud your voice is.

 Use "Silent Magic" to not speak at all without penalty

virtues.name: Skilled Parens
virtues.description: Your parens was more powerful, or a better teacher, than is common. You gain an additional 60 experience points and 30 spell levels during apprenticeship. This Virtue has no effect on your study after apprenticeship, but you still have a close relationship with a powerful magus.

virtues.name: Subtle Magic
virtues.description: You may cast spells without using gestures at no penalty. You gain no benefits from using normal gestures but gain the normal benefit for exaggerated gestures.

virtues.name: Magic Sensitivity
virtues.description: You are often able to identify a place or object as magical. However, your sensitivity makes you more susceptible to magical effects: subtract your Magic Sensitivity score from your Magic Resistance. Choosing this Virtue confers the Ability Magic Sensitivity 1 (page @@).

virtues.name: Hermetic Magus
virtues.description: You are a member of the Order of Hermes. All magi must take this as their Social Status, and only magi may take it.

virtues.name: Improved Characteristics
virtues.description: You have an additional three points to spend on buying Characteristics, but you are still limited to a maximum score of +3 in any single Characteristic unless you take the Virtue Great Characteristic. You may take this Virtue multiple times.

virtues.name: Long-winded
virtues.description:
You can last longer when exerting yourself than 

most, and gain +3 on all your Fatigue rolls. This bonus does not apply to casting spells.

virtues.name: Puissant Code of Hermes
virtues.description: You are particularly adept with one Ability, and add 2 to its value whenever you use it. Note that you do not, in general, use an Ability when learning it, writing about it, or helping someone else to improve it. You may only take this Virtue once for a given Ability, but may take it more than once for different Abilities.

virtues.name: Well-traveled
virtues.description: You have journeyed extensively in this part of the world and find it easy to get along with people throughout the area. You have fifty bonus experience points to spend on living languages, Area Lores, and Bargain, Carouse, Charm, Etiquette, Folk Ken, or Guile.

virtues.name: Fast Caster
virtues.description: Your magic takes less time to perform than that of other magi. You gain +3 to Initiative to cast spells in combat and +3 to rolls to determine fast casting speed.

flaws.name: Restriction
flaws.description: You cannot cast spells at all under certain uncommon conditions. These might refer to your state, such as touching the earth directly or having no beard, or to the target, such as birds or glass, or to your location when you use the magic, such as on a small boat or in a storm. The Restriction also applies to effects generated by any enchanted items you create. Spells cast remain in effect even if

flaws.name: Flawed Parma Magica (Ignem)
flaws.description: Your Parma Magica is defective and provides only half the normal Magic Resistance against a certain Form. You may purchase this Flaw more than once for different Forms.

flaws.name: Short-lived Magic
flaws.description: Your spells do not last as long as they should. Spells that should last a year, last a moon; those of a moon, only to the next sunrise or sundown; and those of a sun, merely Diameter. Diameter, Concentration, Ring, and Momentary spells are not affected.

flaws.name: Enemies
flaws.description: Someone is causing trouble for you, such as a local baron or bishop, a band of outlaws, or a really nasty innkeeper. The enemy must be powerful enough to endanger you — this is best agreed on with the storyguide and the rest of the troupe.

flaws.name: Judged Unfairly
flaws.description: Somehow you come across the wrong way to people, and they universally distrust and underestimate you. You catch no one’s eye, impress no one, and can get no one to take you seriously. If you ever find an exceptional someone who sees you as you want to be seen, you will cling to that person. You cannot gain a positive Reputation in any community, and this Flaw is incompatible with any Virtue that g

flaws.name: Infamous
flaws.description: People know you well and curse you in their prayers. You have a level 4 bad Reputation, specifying the horrible deeds that earned you such ill will.

flaws.name: Creative Block
flaws.description: You have problems creating new things in the lab. You take a –3 penalty to all Lab Totals unless you are using a Laboratory Text or being taught. If you experiment, roll twice as many dice on the experimentation table.

flaws.name: Oversensitive - Minor
flaws.description: Something that others find merely unpleasant you consider intolerable. Examples might include an oversensitivity to disrespect, to slovenliness, or to impiety. If you are the violent type, you may start fights with those who offend you.

spells.name: Demon’s Eternal Oblivion
spells.description: Weakens and possibly destroys a demon. If the spell penetrates the demon’s Magic Resistance, the demon loses Might Score equal to the spell’s level.

spells.name: Disenchant
spells.description: You make a Hermetic magic item lose all its powers permanently if the level of this spell + a stress die (no botch) equals or exceeds the highest level of the enchantments in the item. The enchantment is utterly destroyed, as is all of the vis that was used in the magic item. The object left is in a

spells.name: Opening the Intangible Tunnel
spells.description: You can open a magical channel from yourself to some target, allowing you to cast any spell with a range greater than Personal on that target. The tunnel does not, of itself, grant any sense impressions of the target — you must cast appropriate spells through it if you wish to see. Spells cast throu

spells.name: Watching Ward
spells.description: Watching Ward puts another spell on a given target on hold until that spell is triggered by a simple condition, which is determined when this ritual is cast. The target of the Watching Ward must be present for the entire casting ritual. When the conditions you specify come to pass, the suspended spe

spells.name: Wizard’s Sidestep
spells.description: Your image appears up to 1 pace from where you actually are, so attacks aimed there are likely to miss you. Whenever the image is successfully struck, it disappears and reappears in another spot. In combat, early attacks are aimed at the image, and so automatically miss you. Once the image has been

spells.name: The Call to Slumber
spells.description: The target becomes sleepy and falls asleep within a few seconds.

spells.name: Abrading Stones
spells.description: This spell lifts all loose rocks and pebbles in a 15-pace radius about the target, and grinds them against the victim. Damage is +5 per round.

spells.name: Pilum of Fire
spells.description: A 2-foot, thick, spear-shaped jet of fire flies from your palms, doing +15 damage to the individual it hits.

spells.name: Wizard’s Leap
spells.description: The caster instantly transports himself up to 50 paces in any direction, provided he can see his destination or has an Arcane Connection to it. His Talisman comes with him automatically but casting requisites are required to bring along any other clothing or equipment. This spell is very effective a

spells.name: Seven-League Stride
spells.description: Transports you to any place within seven leagues either that you can see or that you have an Arcane Connection with.
